description: Composite key (date, line_code, sku_id) has 8 duplicate records forming 4 duplicate pairs. The data model expects unique records per date-line-sku combination, but rows [15,16], [38,39], [62,63], and [89,90] (0-based) share identical composite keys. This represents 6.7% duplicate rate (8/120 rows). Sampling shows duplicates have identical field values (produced_qty, defect_rate), indicating ETL duplicate extraction rather than legitimate versioned records. Single-column distinct_count checks would miss this as each individual column (date, line_code, sku_id) has acceptable cardinality; only the composite key reveals the duplication.
detection_hints: d02-duplicate-key skill Step 3: After identifying that neither date, line_code, nor sku_id alone should be unique (time-series with multiple lines and SKUs), check composite key (date, line_code, sku_id) distinct count vs row_count. Duplicate rows have matching values across all fields, confirming redundant records rather than update/versioning scenario.

evidence.field_value_match: all duplicate pairs have identical field values across all columns
